provenance: What each class contributes to a split, as parts. Transcribed from each class file's `## Dip value` section plus its subclass table. WORKED EXAMPLE ONLY — Rogue and Fighter are populated so the shape can be checked; the other fifteen classes are not yet written. Composition feeds the split *filter*, never a published number: see SKILL.md.

schema.id: `<class>/<levels>` for the class-generic part, `<class>/<levels>/<subclass>` for a subclass-specific one. A build takes the generic part AND at most one subclass part at the same level.
schema.as_first: Applies only when this class is the character's LEVEL 1 class. Exactly one class in a split is first. Saving throws and the good armour come from here and nowhere else.
schema.as_dip: Applies when the class is entered after level 1. Same levels, much less: no saving throws, reduced armour, one skill instead of four.
schema.grants: SET-VALUED, never summed. `prof` unions into the save set and is then scored by derive_saves(); `armour` takes the best category across all parts; `shield` is a boolean OR; `skills` and `expertise` sum but feed the skl rubric rather than an axis directly.
schema.deltas: The genuinely additive part, in axis rungs. Summed across parts, then clamped to 0-5. These are FILTER-GRADE estimates.
schema.requires: Condition on the rest of the build, or null. `{"primary": "cha"}` means the part is worth its deltas only on a Charisma body; otherwise deltas are halved.
schema.conflicts: Tags this part competes for. Two parts sharing a tag do not stack — the larger delta applies and the smaller is dropped. `bonus-action-attack` is capped by Lone Wolf's two Bonus Actions; `extra-attack` never stacks.
schema.exit: What the class gives up by stopping at N levels instead of 20. Keyed by the level stopped at. Applied to the PRIMARY class only, since a dip never had those levels to lose.

conflict_tags.extra-attack: Extra Attack does not stack from two sources.
conflict_tags.bonus-action-attack: Lone Wolf grants two Bonus Actions; a third source has nowhere to go.
conflict_tags.expertise: Expertise on the same skill twice is wasted; the skl rubric saturates.
conflict_tags.sneak-attack: One Sneak Attack per turn regardless of source.

rogue/1.note: The Expertise argument is about Rogue 1, not the dip. Multiclassing *into* Rogue grants light armour and one skill, no Expertise.

rogue/2.note: Cunning Action: Dash / Disengage / Hide as a Bonus Action.

rogue/3.note: The standard Rogue dip: Cunning Action plus a subclass. Sneak Attack 2d6.

rogue/3/Thief.note: A second Bonus Action, on top of Lone Wolf's extra one. The strongest three-level dip in the list.

rogue/3/Assassin.note: Action and Bonus Action restored at the start of combat; guaranteed crits on the surprised.

rogue/3/Swashbuckler.note: Sneak Attack with no advantage and no adjacent ally required.

rogue/3/Inquisitive.note: Insightful Fighting as a repeatable Sneak Attack enabler.

rogue/5.note: Extends the dip to Uncanny Dodge and Cunning Strike.

rogue/9.note: Sneak Attack 5d6, Evasion at 7, second Expertise pair at 6, subclass feature at 9. At-will damage, so endurance rises.

fighter/1.note: Heavy armour and shields even as a dip; Second Wind. Str+Con saves only when first.

fighter/2.note: Action Surge. The single best two levels for action economy in the list.

fighter/11.note: Improved Extra Attack — three attacks per Action, six per round under Lone Wolf — plus the off-cadence feat at 11.

fighter/11/Battle Master.note: Superiority dice on the short-rest clock; manoeuvres carry riders and control.
